patch.description:
Partially updates a Rock. Only the fields provided in the request body will be changed, and the response is the complete Rock as it now stands.

Completion is tracked from `statusCode`, exactly as it is in the app: setting `DONE` marks the Rock `completed` and stamps `completedDate`, and moving off `DONE` clears both. Send `statusCode` to complete a Rock - `completed` and `completedDate` are not writable.

`userId` reassigns the owner and must name an active user in the authenticated user's company (`GET /users`). `teamId` and `additionalTeamIds` must name Teams available to them (`GET /teams/available`). Both mirror what the app allows; either one outside those bounds is rejected rather than applied.

`teamId` and every entry in `additionalTeamIds` must be a Team available to the authenticated user - the same Teams `GET /teams/available` returns, which is what the app offers in its Team picker. Anything else is rejected rather than filed somewhere the company cannot see it.

Returns an array because the underlying create takes a list of owners; this endpoint always sends exactly one, so the array holds exactly one Rock.

Pass `email` to look one person up by address; an address nobody in the company uses returns an empty array rather than an error.

get.description: Returns the soonest upcoming Meeting for the given Team, together with its agenda sections and the Team roster, so a caller has everything needed to prepare. Only the near term is considered - roughly the next month for most companies, longer for some - so a 404 means nothing is scheduled soon, not that the Team never meets.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: The Id of the Team whose next Meeting to return. Discoverable via `GET /teams`.

404.description: No upcoming Meeting is scheduled for this Team

get.summary: Get the next Meeting for a Team

get.description: Returns a page of the Team's concluded Meetings, most recent first, each with the ratings its attendees gave, how long it ran and how many of its Issues it worked. The collection is past Meetings only - the upcoming one has its own route at `/meetings/next`. `meetingType` selects one kind of Meeting per call and defaults to `level10`, the Weekly Meeting. Notes and the items a Meeting worked are not included here - read one Meeting by its Id for those. A Team that has never met returns an empty page, not a 404. Callers who are neither an Owner nor an Admin can only read Teams they belong to; the core API answers 403 for the rest.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: The Id of the Team whose past Meetings to return. Discoverable via `GET /teams`.

parameters.name: meetingType
parameters.description: Which kind of Meeting to return. The core API filters to exactly one kind per call, so reading a Team's Weekly Meetings and its Quarterlies takes two calls. `level10` is the Weekly Meeting. An annual session is stored as two chained documents, and a past read only ever returns the second: `annualDayOne` and `annualDayTwo` both select the same day-two rows, because the core API rewrites the former to the latter for past Meetings. `other` is the one exception to one-kind-per-call: it is a catch-all for everything that is not a Weekly, Quarterly or Annual Meeting, so it returns Focus Days, Vision Building days, One-on-Ones and custom Meetings together.

parameters.name: pageIndex
parameters.description: Which page to return, counting from 0

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: How many Meetings to return per page

get.description: Returns one concluded Meeting with the notes taken during it and the Headlines, cascading messages, Issues, To-Dos and Rocks it worked. Notes are the only free-text record of what was decided - Ninety has no separate decisions field. Same visibility rules as the history list.

parameters.name: meetingId
parameters.description: The Id of the Meeting to return

400.description: The Meeting Id is not a 24-character hex Id

404.description: No Meeting exists with this Id

get.description: Returns the Team's Vision/Traction Organizer alongside the leadership Team's, each trimmed to the Core Values, the Core Focus, and the 1-Year Plan and 3-Year Picture goals. Only what the caller can see in the app is returned - leadership sections that have not been shared come back empty. A Team that has never filled its V/TO in returns empty sections rather than an error.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: The Id of the Team whose V/TO to return. Discoverable via `GET /teams`.

get.description: Returns the company's Accountability Chart: every Seat, what that Seat is accountable for, and the people sitting in it. Use it to answer who owns a given area of the business and who to route work to. `seats` is flat and ordered top-down - a Seat always precedes the Seats reporting to it, and siblings keep the order the app draws them in - so rebuild the hierarchy from `parentSeatId`, which is absent on the top Seat. Each holder carries the `userId` that the To-Do and Issue create endpoints accept, so a Seat ties straight through to `/users`. A Seat with no holders is a real state: the Seat exists and nobody fills it. A company that has never set its chart up returns an empty `seats` array rather than a 404. Only the primary company chart is returned; personal and shared charts are not exposed. Every Seat carries `name` and `responsibilities[].name`; pass `seatIds` to also get `id` and `description` on those Seats' responsibilities - omit it and every Seat keeps the trimmed summary shape.

parameters.name: seatIds
parameters.description: Scopes the chart to these Seats plus each one's ancestor chain, instead of every Seat on the chart. Each named Seat's `responsibilities` carry full detail (`id` and `description`); an ancestor pulled in only for tree structure keeps the trimmed summary shape. Omit to list every Seat with the summary shape. An Id not on the chart fails the call rather than being silently dropped.

get.description: Returns a page of the Headlines on one Team's list - the short good-news and bad-news notes a Team raises in its Meetings. `teamId` is required: Headlines belong to exactly one Team and there is no cross-Team read. Headlines already discussed are left out unless `includeDiscussed` is set, and archived ones are a separate list reached with `archived`. Cascading Messages live in the same collection and are returned only when `isCascadedMessage` is set - the two kinds are never mixed in one response. A Team with nothing on its list returns an empty page, not a 404. Callers who are neither an Owner nor an Admin can only read Teams they belong to; the core API answers 403 for the rest.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: The Id of the Team whose Headlines to return. Discoverable via `GET /teams/available`.

parameters.name: isCascadedMessage
parameters.description: Return Cascading Messages instead of Headlines. The two share one collection and are never mixed in a response: this selects which kind you get.

parameters.name: includeDiscussed
parameters.description: Also return Headlines that have already been discussed. Discussed Headlines are left out by default, which is what the app shows.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Return archived Headlines instead of active ones. Archiving is separate from being discussed, so this is a different list rather than a wider one.

parameters.name: searchText
parameters.description: Free-text search across the title and body

parameters.name: pageIndex
parameters.description: Which page to return, counting from 0

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: How many Headlines to return per page

400.description: teamId is missing or is not a 24-character hex Id

403.description: The authenticated User may not read the requested Team

post.description: Creates a Headline on one Team, where it appears on that Team's list exactly as one created in the app does, and notifies its followers. `title` is the Headline itself and `description` an optional HTML body. Owned by the authenticated User unless `userId` names someone else in the same company - a User outside it is rejected with a 403. Either way the authenticated User is recorded as the creator. Set `isCascadedMessage` to create a Cascading Message instead.

403.description: The authenticated User may not create Headlines for this Team, or named an owner outside their company
